title: The Mysterious Migrant Potters of Ancient Tampa Bay - Nautilus
gist: A study in American Antiquity, based on century-old pottery shards, finds evidence that Mississippian-culture migrants reached as far south as Tampa Bay, extending the known range of the mound-building culture (c. 1,000-1,600 CE).

insights.claim: A new American Antiquity study finds the first compelling evidence that Mississippian-culture migrants ranged as far south as Tampa Bay.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Low direct investment relevance; illustrates reanalysis of old collections yielding new findings.
insights.quote: a new study published in American Antiquity finds compelling evidence of Mississippian migrants ranging as far south as Tampa Bay for the first time

insights.claim: University of Florida and Florida Museum of Natural History anthropologists reached the conclusion by restudying pottery shards excavated nearly a century ago, which bore elaborate Mississippian decorations unlike the plain earthenware of the local Safety Harbor culture.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Shows value locked in existing archival/museum datasets awaiting new analysis.
insights.quote: meticulously studying pottery shards recovered from the area nearly a century ago
insights.locator: Anthropologists from the University of Florida

insights.claim: Mississippian cultural variants flourished for centuries across the midwestern and southeastern US, from about 1,000 to around 1,600 CE.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.quote: several of these cultural variants flourished for centuries, from 1,000 to around 1,600 CE
